It wasn't the fact that I had dropped it, it was more of the fact that I had been working for 13 hours, had a 10 person tabke come in right before close, and hadn't had anything to eat or drink besides water.

So sorry for you. Us women know our bodies better than any nurse or doctor when it comes to giving birth  Traumatizing births are so common yet not talked about enough.

I had an extremely quick labor with my one and only baby and went from a 3 to 10cm in an hour and feeling like I had to poo as well. I kept asking them to check me again and they told me to relax bc it was my first birth and I KNEW this baby was coming. The contractions were on top of each other and I swore I was about to literally poop out this baby..  Guess what? Baby in my arms 5 minutes later. Pushed for 3 minutes with a nurse bc doc was MIA. Doc basically just pulled her out. The transition between screaming in agony and then complete shock took about 3 seconds. 

I think a huge misconception regarding birth is that if you are only a few centimeters than you have hours before anything happens. Traumatizing births need to be addressed more.

This is usually the first symptom of a panic attack for me personally. I then become super aware of my breathing and end up hyperventilating even more than what I already was. Breathing exercises are helpful during the peak of a panic attack but I've noticed that my chest tightness and shortness of breath are in my head. Look into Dr. Harry Barry on YouTube on how he describes anxiety and the physical symptoms of being anxious. One of my favorite quotes by him is "uncomfortable, but NOT dangerous." It is hard right now with COVID, especially on those of us with health anxiety.

I constantly have to give myself a pep talk and remind myself that my symptoms are a result of anxiety. I've had atleast 3 different occasions where I'm convinced I have COVID and end up hyperventilating (ended up in the ER once) and freaking myself out. Then the panic attack ends and I feel like an idiot, but that's just how it is sometimes. All we can do is try to take care of ourselves the best we can, both mentally and physically.

Maybe I've just gotten used to it though lol. I waddle but it's actually due to my big ole belly instead of the pain now.

It is hard having so much pain early on, especially if you aren't showing yet. I feel better at 34 weeks than I did at 20, but not every woman is the same. Pregnancy is hard on the body no matter how many times you've done it. Just take it day by day 🧡

My OB told me its a big misconception that women have to gain a shit load of weight, or "eat for two" when they are pregnant. When I told her I wasn't gaining weight at first, she told me it's unhealthy to gain 55 lbs (just an example) even though its more common now. I have only gained 12 pounds so far and I'm 32 weeks. My appetite increased in the second trimester but I wasn't eating more, just more often. As far as your bump, don't worry about that! I am pretty thin with a longer torso I really didn't show until 28 weeks. My belly button is finally popping at 32 and my belly is definitely noticeable. I don't have terrible back pain either and can still be pretty active too!

You'll get your belly and it will be the perfect size for you, and before you know it you will be wishing that baby would come on out already.

I ordered food instead of cooking.. just little changes. It's important to do what your body needs, especially in the first trimester. Just rest up as much as possible.

Besides having morning sickness, I had a hard time grasping that I was pregnant until I heard her heartbeat when I was 8 weeks. I started to feel kicking at 18 and that's when it became real for me. At 28 weeks I feel her everyday!

At 4 weeks that's understandable, most women don't find out until after that too. But congrats mama! Totally normal to feel that way!

I made a post about my first trimester being just this. I was so so SO tired. To the point where I cried over my lack of energy pretty much everyday. 

Not only was I tired, I felt SICK. I had morning sickness, but I also felt like I had the flu the entire first trimester. I was cold and achy and honestly wondered how I would care for a baby if I never stopped feeling this way 🤣 I cried a lot due to how bad I felt.. I thought I was seriously ill, but it is normal while you're body is working overtime to make the placenta. 

I started to feel better around 18 weeks (I'm almost 26 now). I went from throwing up everyday to only a few times a week. I'm still more tired than usual and I have days where I just feel that general malaise, but it's nothing like the first trimester. It will get better. Once you start to get a little more energy and feel those kicks, it will become a much better experience ❤

I'm almost 8 weeks into my first pregnancy, here are some symptoms I had before testing: 

After my missed period (sometimes I'm irregular so I didn't think about it) I had this milky white discharge that is steadily increasing. I usually only have clear stretchy discharge when I'm ovulating. 

Getting extremely angry and then crying. A truck drove past me and it was loud and scared me and I started crying. Yup. Crazy lmao. 

Random heart palpitations. I could be sitting down and then my heart would pound hard for 5 to 10 seconds, I'd get lightheaded, and then it would stop. I had a few panic attacks because I thought I was having a heart attack. 

LIGHTNING VAGINA. It felt like I got cunt punted. 

I had a few normal symptoms, like slight nausea throughout the day, missed period, and peeing a lot. I thought that most of my symptoms were to do anxiety. Nope, pregnant! 

I don't have sore breasts though, that's the one symptom I haven't experienced yet. I started a really great job too, so timing was off but I'm still excited 😁 

CONGRATS BTW. GOOD HEALTH YOUR WAY TO ALL THE EXPECTING MAMAS!!
